newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil closes down $5 at lows, Brent $17.77.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil closes down $5 at lows, Brent $17.77.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures closed down $5 at the day's lows on Wednesday on steady technical selling inspired by bearish API figures, traders said.
The front month July settled at $158.75 a tonne, while August closed at $160.25.
Brokers said July tumbled after breaking key technical support at $159.50 and $159.75.
"It's graveyard numbers. It looks terrible, and we should have more technical selling tomorrow," a broker said.
The August Brent crude futures contract was trading down 31 cents at August $17.77 a barrel.
Brokers noted that in New York heating oil had not reflected gas oil's weakness. It traded at $51.55 cents a gallon above the bottom end of its range at 51.30 cents.
"Gas oil looks far worse than anything else at the moment," one broker said. "It's been good technical selling on the back of essentially bearish API figures."
Brokers said EIA weekly stocks figures mostly confirmed American Petroleum Institute data showing a build in gasoline stocks and a decline in crude stocks.

The API figures also showed U.S. crude oil imports for the week ended June 13 hit a record 9.4 million barrels per day (bpd), up nearly a million barrels per day. At the same time, gasoline output set a record 8.23 million bpd after breaking the record set two weeks prior.

Brokers said the bearish tone derived also from the failure of the gas oil contract to strengthen on Tuesday's rash of bullish stories about Middle East tension and arguments between Iraq and the United Nations over arms inspections and the oil for food programme.
